raw:
{
  "items": [
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "continuum element type and dimensionality",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Sec. 1.3.1 specifies linear hexahedral elements, whereas Sec. 4.1 describes the same cantilever using 150 × 52 × 1 linear quadrilateral elements. The workflow otherwise describes a 2D problem.",
      "readings": [
        "150 × 52 bilinear quadrilateral elements in a 2D continuum; the final ×1 is a nominal thickness count",
        "150 × 52 × 1 trilinear hexahedral elements in a 3D solid"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "material",
      "entity": "elastic constitutive reduction for a quadrilateral model",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "For the 2D interpretation, neither Sec. 2.1 nor Sec. 4.1 specifies plane stress or plane strain. The stated Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio do not resolve this choice.",
      "readings": [
        "Plane stress with the stated E and Poisson's ratio",
        "Plane strain with the stated E and Poisson's ratio"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "domain_extent",
      "entity": "thickness used in continuum topology optimization",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Secs. 2.1 and 4.1 assign 1 cm expressly for size optimization, without specifying the continuum topology thickness. Uniform thickness only scales compliance in a 2D in-plane model, but can affect layout under the unresolved 3D interpretation.",
      "readings": [
        "Use 10 mm thickness in topology optimization as well as subsequent size optimization",
        "Use 1 mm unit thickness in the topology model and 10 mm only for the subsequent frame volume"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_direction",
      "entity": "100 kN point load on the free end",
      "issue": "figure_only",
      "description": "Secs. 2.1 and 4.1 give the magnitude and in-plane position but no direction or force components. These would have to be obtained from the unavailable problem diagram in Fig. 2a.",
      "readings": [
        "Vertical downward, perpendicular to the cantilever span",
        "Horizontal toward the fixed end",
        "In-plane at 45 degrees downward toward the fixed end"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "load_position",
      "entity": "point-load position through the thickness, if hexahedral elements are used",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 2.1 specifies the position 18 cm below the top on the opposite free end, but gives no through-thickness coordinate for the hexahedral interpretation of Sec. 1.3.1.",
      "readings": [
        "At the thickness midplane, z/t = 0.5",
        "On the front surface, z/t = 0",
        "On the rear surface, z/t = 1"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "passive_region",
      "entity": "non-design material near the clamp and point load",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Sec. 2.1 defines no passive-element mask. The pixel tagging described in Secs. 2.2.4 and 4.1 does not establish a continuum topology-optimization density mask or its extent.",
      "readings": [
        "No passive elements; all continuum element densities remain design variables",
        "Keep the two free-end elements immediately above and below the load node solid",
        "Keep a one-element-wide strip along the fixed edge and the two elements adjacent to the load node solid"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "volume_fraction",
      "entity": "volume fraction of the later numerical run identified with this cantilever",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Fig. 2b–d explicitly specify 0.7, 0.5 and 0.3 respectively. The conflict concerns the continuation in Sec. 4.1: Fig. 12's caption says 0.3, while the topology-optimization paragraph says 0.5; Fig. 18b also identifies 0.5.",
      "readings": [
        "Vf = 0.3 for the Sec. 4.1 topology run, following Fig. 12's caption",
        "Vf = 0.5 for the Sec. 4.1 topology run, following its prose and Fig. 18b"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "units and coordinate convention for filter radius R = 1.2",
      "issue": "vague",
      "description": "Fig. 2's caption and Sec. 4.1 give R = 1.2 without units. Eq. (7) uses distances but does not establish whether they are measured in element pitches or physical coordinates.",
      "readings": [
        "R = 1.2 element pitches, equivalent to 12 mm on the reported mesh",
        "R = 1.2 mm when distances are evaluated in the N–mm coordinate system"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "density-filter numerator",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Eq. (6) sums weighted rho_i rather than neighboring rho_j, making the printed filter an identity operation. This conflicts with the stated density regularization and the nonlocal derivative in Eq. (12).",
      "readings": [
        "Implement Eq. (6) literally, so filtered density equals the original density",
        "Replace rho_i in the numerator with rho_j and apply the normalized neighboring-density filter"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "SIMP sensitivity after density filtering",
      "issue": "conflicting",
      "description": "Sec. 1.3.1 says filtered densities replace the original densities in the topology problem, but Eqs. (11) and (13) print the factor p*rho_j^(p-1) without a filter hat.",
      "readings": [
        "Evaluate the SIMP derivative at the filtered physical density, then apply the filter chain rule",
        "Use the unfiltered design density in the printed power factor while assembling stiffness from filtered densities"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "topology optimizer and density-update controls",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "No optimizer or update controls are identified for topology optimization. The MMA and SQP discussion in Sec. 2.4 explicitly concerns subsequent frame size and layout optimization.",
      "readings": [
        "Optimality-criteria updates with a 0.2 absolute density move limit and square-root damping",
        "Optimality-criteria updates with a 0.1 absolute density move limit and square-root damping",
        "MMA with a 0.2 absolute density move limit",
        "SQP with density bounds and the volume constraint"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "initial topology density field",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Secs. 1.3.1, 2.1 and 4.1 do not specify the initial continuum densities.",
      "readings": [
        "Uniform initial density rho_i = Vf",
        "Initially solid domain, rho_i = 1",
        "Perturbed initialization rho_ij = Vf + 0.01*(-1)^(i+j)"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "filter_or_solver_setting",
      "entity": "topology-optimization termination criterion",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Fig. 2 specifies a maximum of 200 iterations, but no topology convergence measure or tolerance. The later tolerances are explicitly for frame size and layout optimization.",
      "readings": [
        "Always execute 200 topology iterations",
        "Stop when maximum absolute density change is below 0.001, or at 200 iterations",
        "Stop when relative compliance change is below 0.0001, or at 200 iterations"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    },
    {
      "category": "mesh",
      "entity": "element integration and stabilization",
      "issue": "missing",
      "description": "Secs. 1.3.1 and 4.1 identify linear elements but do not specify their integration or stabilization formulation.",
      "readings": [
        "Fully integrated elements: 2 × 2 Gauss integration for quadrilaterals or 2 × 2 × 2 for hexahedra",
        "One-point reduced integration with hourglass stabilization"
      ],
      "effect": "layout"
    }
  ]
}
